articles.title: Every Persona Game and Spin-Off in Order
articles.summary: A complete timeline of Shin Megami Tensei's most beloved spin-off.
articles.body:
Beginning its life as a Shin Megami Tensei spin-off, the Persona series has become one of the biggest names in modern RPGs. From multiple major sequels and remakes to anime adaptations and even stage plays, Persona is a multimedia sensation, and its popularity doesn’t seem to be slowing down anytime soon.

With the official announcement of both Persona 4 Revival and Persona 6 , new players are probably wondering where’s the best place to start. Below, we’ll give you a full rundown of every game and spin-off, including the best entry point for newcomers and both the chronological and release order of the series.

In total, there are currently 21 Persona games . Several of these are expanded versions of the mainline entries in the series, whether that’s in the form of re-releases featuring new story content or remakes. While we won’t include direct ports or remasters, we’ll make sure to note every alternate version of each game when listing them below.

Which Persona Game Should You Play First?

If you're looking for the perfect place to start, you can’t really go wrong jumping into Persona 3 Reload or Persona 5 Royal. They’re the latest versions of the third and fifth mainline entries in the series, and are available on PC and every major console.

For those concerned about skipping the story by jumping into later entries in the series, you won’t miss anything by going straight to Persona 3, 4, or 5. Each game tells an entirely new story with original characters that’s largely disconnected from its predecessors, so they’re great launching points for those coming in fresh. To narrow your choices down, I'd recommend taking a look at some gameplay videos, social links, and even the soundtracks across each game to see what "stands out" to you.

Every Persona Game and Spin-Off in Chronological Order

These blurbs contain mild spoilers for each game, including characters, settings, and story beats.

The first game in the series, Revelations: Persona was Atlus’ reaction to the positive reception of Shin Megami Tensei: If… , which was another Shin Megami Tensei spin-off centered around high-schoolers battling demons. Capitalizing on how much players enjoyed the central concept, Revelations: Persona offered a full dungeon-crawling RPG centered around a group of high schoolers battling a supernatural uprising throughout the town of Mikage-cho.

Along the way, they use the powers of their awakened Personas to take down shadows and explore dungeons filled with random encounters, leveling up their party and growing stronger over the course of the game. Revelations: Persona was the foundation of the franchise as we know it today, introducing elements like wielding Personas in combat, the Velvet Room and a teenage cast of heroes.

The second entry in the Persona series, Persona 2: Innocent Sin launched in 1999. The game follows a new set of high-school students led by protagonist Tatsuya Suou, who set out on a mission to take down a mysterious villain known as Joker and the cult of the Masked Circle.

Centring around an evil plot where malicious rumors spreading around the town of Sumaru come to life, Persona 2 once again focuses on exploring dungeons, wielding Personas, fighting shadows and leveling up your party. Unlike other entries in the series, it received a direct sequel just a year later, with Persona 2: Eternal Punishment acting as a continuation of the game's story.

Following up the events of Innocent Sin, Eternal Punishment promoted side character, Maya Amano, to the protagonist role. Sent to write an article about a new rumor regarding a phenomenon known as the Joker Curse, the game quickly sees Maya and her allies rally against a returning foe.

Acting as a direct continuation of Innocent Sin's story, it centers on the same style of turn-based, dungeon-crawling gameplay, as players build their party and wield their Personas to battle shadows.

4. Persona 3 (2006) / Persona 3 FES (2007) / Persona 3 Portable (2009) / Persona 3 Reload (2024)

The third mainline entry in the franchise, Persona 3 was a major evolution of the Persona formula. Opting to focus on its high-school premise, Persona 3 introduced a daily calendar , with one half of the game tasking players with attending school, developing friendships and studying, while the other sent them to fight shadows in the supernatural realm of Tartarus.

The story focuses on high school student Makoto Yuki, who finds he's able to experience a mysterious space of time known as the Dark Hour, where regular people are trapped in coffins and a demonic tower sprouts from his school. Teaming with his classmates, he explores the tower, uncovering a sinister plot that threatens the entire world. Persona 3 is considered a landmark entry for the series, introducing social links, day-to-day activities and many other mechanics that have since become synonymous with the franchise.

5. Persona 3: Dancing in Moonlight (2018)

A rhythm-based dancing spin-off of Persona 3 that takes place during the main campaign, Persona 3: Dancing in Moonlight sees Elizabeth challenge the S.E.E.S team to a dance-off in the Velvet Room. The events of the game are set during a dream but are completely canon to the story, and follow the team performing various dance routines to iconic Persona 3 tracks.

6. Persona 4 (2008) / Persona 4 Golden (2012)

The fourth mainline entry in the Persona series, Persona 4 takes place in the rural town of Inaba. Players assume the role of Yu Narukami: a high schooler from the city who moves to the country to live with his uncle and cousin for a year. After arriving, a string of violent murders begin to take place in the town, as Yu and his friends quickly discover they’re somehow linked to a mysterious otherworldly realm they can access by stepping through TV monitors.

Delving into this mysterious new world, Yu and his friends face supernatural forces as they learn more about the murders, using their powers to try and stop them. Building off the mechanics of Persona 3, Persona 4 once again utilizes the calendar system, as players build social links and attend school while also exploring vast dungeons and defeating enemies with their Personas.

7. Persona Q: Shadow of the Labyrinth (2014)

Technically taking place during the Persona 3 and Persona 4 storylines simultaneously, Persona Q: Shadow of the Labyrinth is a crossover between both games. During the typhoon segment of Persona 3 and the Culture Festival segment of Persona 4, the S.E.E.S team and the Investigation Squad are trapped inside a warped version of Yasogami High School.

The time-bending event sees both teams come together to investigate the strange occurrence and escape back to their respective spots on the timeline. Along the way, players explore a labyrinth filled with new enemies and uncover an original story, with the spin-off acting as a callback to the series’ more traditional dungeon-crawler roots.

A continuation of both Persona 3 and 4’s narratives and the franchise’s first major spin-off, Persona 4 Arena sees Yu Narukami return to Inaba and stumble into a new adventure, as he returns to the TV world for a mysterious fighting tournament. Forced to battle against his allies and a group known as the Shadow Operatives, which is comprised of Persona 3's Mitsuru, Akihiko and Aigis, Arena offers a full fighting game boasting a roster of iconic Persona characters.

A year following the release of Persona 4 Arena, the spin-off received a sequel titled Persona 4 Arena Ultimax . Taking place directly after the events of the first game, the Persona 4 squad teams up with the Shadow Operatives to return to the TV World and battle against the mysterious forces running the fighting tournament. Ultimax was ultimately an upgrade for the first game, bringing in an expanded roster including returning characters like Yukari, Junpei, Ken and Koromaru.

The fourth and arguably most unexpected spin-off of Persona 4, Persona 4: Dancing All Night is a rhythm-based dancing game where the Investigation Squad performs routines to iconic Persona tracks. It offers a completely canon continuation of the storyline, following Yu and the team as they’re sucked into an alternate dimension known as the Midnight Stage.

11. Persona 5 (2016) / Persona 5 Royal (2019)

The fifth mainline entry in the series, Persona 5 hit shelves in Japan in 2016 before launching worldwide in 2017. Taking players to Tokyo, it casts them as a new protagonist known as Joker, who finds himself on probation after being framed for a crime he didn’t commit. Attending the local high school, Joker and his friends discover a supernatural alternate dimension, which allows them to infiltrate mystical palaces and change the hearts of evil-doers around the city.

Before long, the group becomes notorious on the streets of Tokyo, going under the alias of the Phantom Thieves. The game builds heavily off the formula established by Persona 3 and 4, including massive story-focused levels that unfold over a month, the return of the negotiation system and a new dungeon system known as Mementos . Persona 5 launched the franchise into the stratosphere, quickly becoming Atlus' best-selling game of all time and cultivating a huge fan base.

12. Persona Q2: New Cinema Labyrinth (2018)

A sequel to Persona Q: Shadow of the Labyrinth, New Cinema Labyrinth once again depicts a crossover between various Persona characters. After the Phantom Thieves find themselves trapped in a movie theater, they ally with Persona 3's S.E.E.S team and Persona 4's Investigation Squad to find an escape, traveling into the movies on the screen in an attempt to fix their endings.

Much like the original game, Persona Q2 simultaneously takes place during the Persona 3, 4 and 5 storylines, with the adventure pulling each group out of their respective timeline. There, they explore dungeons from a first-person perspective and fight turn-based battles against various enemies.

Taking place during the events of Persona 5, Persona 5 Tactica is a strategy-focused spin-off that’s similar in style to the XCOM franchise. The story follows the Phantom Thieves mysteriously traveling to an alternate realm known as the Kingdoms. Unable to escape, Joker and Morgana are forced to abandon the rest of the Phantom Thieves after they're brainwashed by the realm's monstrous ruler, Tyrant Marie, forcing the pair to begin an adventure to save their allies and return home.

Along the way, they team up with the local resistance, helping them fight against Tyrant Marie's forces. The game revolves around a tactical grid-based combat system, as players direct three units across the battlefield and take out enemies.

14. Persona 5: Dancing in Starlight (2018)

Atlus’ third rhythm-based dancing spin-off, Persona 5: Dancing in Starlight sees Caroline and Justine bring the Phantom Thieves to the Velvet Room and challenge them to a dance off. There, the group perform dance routines to several of Persona 5's catchiest tracks.

A spin-off set four months after the events of Persona 5, Strikers sees the Phantom Thieves reunite for a summer vacation. However, the team find themselves sucked into the Metaverse after using an app known as EMMA. Escaping with the help of a new ally, the team don their Phantom Thieves gear once more and set out to discover the truth behind EMMA, the Metaverse, and what it means for the people of Tokyo.

Persona 5 Strikers is a crossover with the long-running Dynasty Warriors franchise, introducing real-time combat to the series. Battles center around the Phantom Thieves taking on large hordes of enemies, which they can deal with through combos or by calling on Personas.

The most recent Persona release is yet another spin-off of Persona 5. This one's a bit funky. Developed by Black Wings Game Studio, Persona 5: The Phantom X is a free-to-play game with microtransactions (otherwise known as a gacha gama) that takes place in 'alternate timeline' to Persona 5 itself. You take on the role of Wonder, a high school student who, of course, awakens his Persona and gains access to the Metaverse.

After the massive success of Metaphor: ReFantazio (it picked up quite a few awards ), Sega announced their desire to keep investing in Atlus, and the Persona IP in particular, in a developers' Q&A session.

Persona 4 Revival was announced at a the 2025 Xbox Showcase , a new remake of the game that originally released on PS2 in 2008 before being remastered as Persona 4 Golden in 2012. The remake is scheduled for release on February 18, 2027, and will be available Day One on Xbox Game Pass.

That's not all. We finally have confirmation that Persona 6 is real . A short teaser gives us a glimpse at least at some cool aesthetics in classic Atlus style, and there's no word on a release date. But it's real! Here's a breakdown of everything we know so far , which includes, in classic Atlus fashion, some good ol' leaks .

In the meantime, the Phantom Thieves from P5R continue to pop up in pretty much every franchising opportunity they can, most recently as skins in Overwatch 2 . Outside of games, Netflix has confirmed development on a live-action Persona TV show . Interesting, I know.

Callum Williams is a freelance media writer with years of experience as a game critic, news reporter, guides writer and features writer.

articles.title: The Classic Carcassonne Board Game Drops to Its Lowest Price in Years
articles.body:
Interested in getting your feel wet in the world of tabletop gaming but overwhelmed by the seeming endless selection of board games out there? I'd recommend starting with the tried-and-true classics. Carcassonne was first released way back in 2000 and over two decades and millions of sold copies later, it's still a highly recommended board game for newcomers. Carcassonne normally retails for $41.99, but right now Bullseye Deals via eBay has it on sale for a mere $14.99 with free shipping. This is the best price I've seen in recent years; the lowest price on Amazon was $17 and that was back in 2024.

Note: "Bullseye Deals" is Target's authorized liquidator. Most of its products (including this board game) ship from Upper Marlboro, Maryland, the same location as Target's main distribution center. The account has well over a million reviews.

Carcassonne Drops to the Lowest Price in Years

Carcassonne is a classic tile placement strategy board game for two to five players and an average playtime of around 35 minutes. During each turn, a player draws and places landscape tiles, which includes roads, cities, fields, and monasteries. Each player can also deploy up to seven meeples to claim features and score points. For example, a farmer tills a field, monks inhabit monasteries, knights guard cities, and highwaymen lurk on roads. Like any good board game, Carcassonne is a mostly strategic game with a healthy dose of luck, so every game is different and there is tons of replayability. It's also a great game for newcomers because the rules are simple and the gameplay is intuitive. It's easy to get into it but takes time to master.

articles.title: Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 Get Preorder Discounts at Amazon (Out Friday)
articles.summary: Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 aren't even out yet, but Amazon is already offering discounts on preorders.
articles.body:
Apple introduced new versions of the standard and Ultra Apple Watch at the Surprise and Shine event last week. Both are now up for preorder, with a release date of September 18 (that’s this Friday). However, Amazon is offering a preorder discount on these devices. You can save $9 on an Apple Watch Series 12 or $19 on an Apple Watch Ultra 4 . These aren’t huge discounts, but if you were planning on buying one at launch anyway, you might as well save a few bucks, right?

Apple Watch Series 12 (GPS + Cellular, 42mm)

The deal is available on the 42mm Apple Watch Series 12, on both GPS and Cellular models. The Series 12 offers everything found in previous models, plus what Apple is calling “the most accurate heart rate sensing in a wearable.” It also has 24-hour battery life with normal use, and you can get up to 12 hours of use on a 15-minute fast-charge.

Apple Watch Ultra 4 (GPS + Cellular, 49mm)

Apple Watch Ultra 4 is a more rugged device that’s designed for workout enthusiasts and outdoorsy types. This one only comes in one size (49mm) and it always has both GPS and cellular connectivity built in. It’s designed to track all sorts of fitness, from hiking in the wilderness to triathlons, from strength training to mountain biking.

The Ultra 4 is said to have “multi-day” battery life, with up to 45 hours of “Max Extended Workout” tracking. It also features fast-charge technology that gets you up to 18 hours of use in just 15 minutes.

All of these models also feature one of the coolest new technologies Apple has introduced this year: audio intelligence. When enabled, this can transcribe the last 15 seconds of audio it detected, letting you catch up if you miss something someone says. It can also summarize conversations, meetings, or lectures using Siri Recap.

These are iterative upgrades, but Apple Watches have gotten relatively iterative upgrades across every generation . And since most people don't buy a new one each year, the upgrades add up over time.

As for the deal on these upcoming Apple Watch models, they're pretty minor discounts, percentage-wise. But these watches aren’t even out yet, so it’s somewhat surprising to find any discount, anywhere. If you were planning to buy one of these new Apple Watches anyway, you might as well get it at Amazon and save $9 or $19.

Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's LEGO coverage and maintains the upcoming release dates articles for video games , LEGO sets , and 4K Blu-rays . You can follow him on Bluesky .

articles.title: Former Tekken Director Katsuhiro Harada Says His Next Game Will Be a ‘Surprise,’ But Not Outside Fans’ Expectations
articles.summary: Katsuhiro Harada, former leader of the Tekken franchise, is finally revealing some details about his next game currently in the works at his independent development house, VS Studio.
articles.body:
Katsuhiro Harada, former leader of the Tekken franchise, is finally revealing some details about his next game currently in the works at his independent development house, VS Studio.

Harada famously exited Bandai Namco earlier this year, leaving his decades-long post at the company as Tekken’s guiding force to make his own studio. A subsidiary of SNK, VS Studio has been slowly building its ranks over the last few months, snagging several former members of Tekken’s key development staff.

And while he’s been pretty quiet about what exactly VS Studio is cooking up, he shed some light on its current projects in a September 2026 interview with VideoGamesChronicle , and it’s tentatively looking like good news for fans of his previous games.

When asked if VS Studio’s next game would be a fighting game, or if the development house aims to be a “genre-agnostic” company, Harada had this to say: “What I can say is that there are some members who I have worked with in the past who have joined the company, but this is purely voluntary.

“...the title that we are creating has not been disclosed, but as I said earlier, I don’t want to betray our fans’ expectations. The game that we’re developing will be some kind of surprise, but rest assured, it is not something that is outside of expectations,” he answered.

While this statement doesn’t affirm anything, it does point to the fact that Harada is making something that is at least somewhat in the realm of what fans are expecting — and that, to us, sounds a lot like a fighting game. (It's also worth noting that Harada himself said he wanted to develop a new fighting game in an interview with Den-fami Nico Gamer after the news of VS Studio was first announced.) Whether it’s a totally new IP or a new installment of an existing franchise remains to be seen, but SNK’s chief publishing officer, Ozan Kocoglu, says VS Studio isn’t opposed to both making original titles and expanding on their previous works.

“I think it can be both. I don’t think we should be limited to one road or the other. I think Harada-san can bring a wealth of experience into supporting our existing IPs in growing in a different way, or going to the next stage alongside people like Oda-san. But at the same time, as SNK is growing to become much bigger and a new company, we also need fresh ideas,” he said.

“We also need to build new IP pillars that, you know, he could be working on, so that they can actually enrich the SNK portfolio beyond what we have. I definitely see Harada-san being able to do both, and it will depend on what he wants to do and how, and especially on which IP he could collaborate on with some of our development leads in the future.”

Kocoglu revealed that SNK is in a period of “aggressive growth,” saying the company needs a “fresh perspective” in order to keep moving forward. He also sees “no reason” why VS Studio should be a “one-off” for SNK, calling Harada a “great addition in terms of DNA with what we’ve been building so far.”

“But do we want to stop at only VS Studio? I don’t think that’s the idea. I think it’s going to be, okay, what are the new opportunities we can find in the market? How do we want to grow as a company? Personally, I think SNK has a strong DNA in action-related games. So anyone who makes an action-related project could potentially join us in the future on a case-by-case basis,” he added.

Harada went on to say that VS Studio has a “very high level of freedom,” and that while the team can “create anything we want,” they’re still beholden to what fans and players expect of them.

“What I want to protect is what I’m good at, as well as meet the expectations that my fans have. On top of that, I also want to collaborate with SNK. We can share the video game expertise that we have and enhance our strengths for both of us in terms of the ways to create video games. So, focusing on what I’m good at, keeping in mind player expectations as well, and having close collaboration with SNK,” he said.

Harada also opened up about his thoughts on the future of the Tekken franchise now that he’s left Bandai Namco, revealing that he’s been mentoring existing members of its staff while he works to grow VS Studio.

“I have no knowledge of what Tekken has in store after my departure, so I think it would be great if you could all reach out to Bandai Namco. For now, I can only speculate, like how fans are speculating as well. But one thing I can say is that I have been working hard to mentor the team members of Tekken, and I can guarantee that the members who are still working on it have evolved and grown. So I’m looking forward to the future of Tekken as a fan.”

Tekken 8 , it seems, is joining the ranks of other mainline fighting games who are adding wildcard guest characters to their rosters, with Baki's Yujiro Hanma set to join the fight in early 2027. We got the chance to interview Tekken series chief producer Naoya Yasuda about why the team chose this character and how in the world they plan on balancing the game around the 'strongest man on earth' when he finally drops next year.

articles.title: Marvel's Wolverine Lets You Have Full Control Over Slow-Motion Options for Cinematic Gameplay
articles.summary: Marvel's Wolverine has an option that lets you control the speed of the game, allowing for hyper-cinematic slow motion action.
articles.body:
Marvel's Wolverine has an option that lets you control the speed of the game, allowing for hyper-cinematic slow-motion action.

Insomniac Games has created an expansive accessibility menu for Marvel's Wolverine, and in it, there's an option to control game speed. You can map this to any button you want on your controller, allowing you to toggle between normal speed and whatever secondary speed you want. One player chose to map this to their D-pad, allowing them to slow the game down to 30%, creating a slow-motion effect. This allows you to have more control over how the action is presented in the game and create more cinematic moments, letting a splash of blood slowly wash across the screen or have Wolverine drill his claws into an enemy before ramping the speed back up.

It's very Zack Snyder-y, as the ex-DC director is well-known for his slow-motion action shots that indulge in violence. Insomniac's last superhero game, Marvel's Spider-Man 2, also included this option. It allowed fans to capture beautiful web-swinging gameplay where time can briefly slow to highlight a graceful animation or a gorgeous shot. It's certainly a great way for creators to have full control over their gameplay for unique footage.

Marvel's Wolverine is officially out now after an extensive five-year wait. IGN gave the game a 6/10 in its review , noting that the game has strong bones, but lacks enough variety to sustain itself.

"Marvel's Wolverine's slick and satisfying combat wears thin well before its conclusion, so much so that even its strong character work can't quite save it from being anything more than okay," we said.

Insomniac Games has noted that it is listening to feedback from players in an effort to keep refining the experience and making it better after launch. Wolverine actor Liam McIntyre has managed to shrug off some of the harsh comments thrown at the game, stating that he's experienced backlash before and is proud of the game that the team made.

articles.title: Masahiro Sakurai Forced to Abandon Game Designers Award After 16 Years as He Can't Find a Successor
articles.summary: Masahiro Sakurai revealed that the Game Designers Award won’t return to the Japan Game Awards, as he has failed to find an adequate replacement to take up his mantle.
articles.body:
Masahiro Sakurai revealed that the Game Designers Award won’t return to the Japan Game Awards, as he has failed to find an adequate replacement to take up his mantle.

The Game of the Year Division of the Japan Game Awards took place yesterday, September 14, recognizing the best and brightest in Japanese game development. While numerous titles and creative minds were celebrated, one accolade is standing out from the rest — and that’s because it’s not coming back for future JGA shows.

Masahiro Sakurai, creator of Kirby and Super Smash Bros., founded the Game Designers Award in 2010. As told by the CESA’s official website , this award recognizes games based on their creativity and originality. Games that are considered for the award must incorporate “new ideas that are a clear departure from existing works” and “expand the form of game software by presenting new ways for the user to enjoy and play with the game.”

Super Smash Bros Ultimate - Sakurai Trailer Screenshots

The Game Designers Award is ultimately granted to “the title that reached out to a wide range of people, including those who don't usually play games actively, and that made the memorable achievement of the year, will be selected as the award-winning title.”

This year, that title was Word Game , a project from independent studio Team9. Word Game is a text-based puzzle game originally made with Traditional Chinese characters, but was localized for Japanese players — something that impressed the judging committee (made up of eleven members of industry veterans like Hideki Kamiya, Yoko Taro, Toby Fox, and more) so much that it won the Game Designers Award.

“This work won by an overwhelming majority of votes even in the second round of judging, where the selection was narrowed down to specific titles,” the CESA’s website says. “Even more astonishingly, while the game seems like it could only work in Japanese, it is actually a localized version of a Traditional Chinese title. I am sure it took advanced skills and clever solutions to complete the transmission. I believe this unique and inimitable game is a fitting choice for the final Game Designers Award.”

Sadly, Word Game will be the last title to receive this accolade at the Japan Game Awards, as Sakurai has not yet found a suitable replacement to help him sift through future contenders. He explained the situation during a presentation at this year's awards ceremony , where he gave some insightful perspective on the industry.

“It’s been 16 years since we started [this award],” he said, as per a live translator. “This is the last year that we’re doing it, and the reason is because there’s nobody who’s going to replace me. That is the only reason. In order to keep this award something that is really convincing and fulfills the role, it needs to be given by somebody who's a director, who's come up with innovative games that have changed gameplay a lot. I scouted and tried to find someone to replace me. I did some presentations to try to find somebody, too. I searched for a couple years, but nobody stepped up to replace me. There’s a lot of other judges, but none of them were able to pick up the mantle.

“Game development is always an experiment, but you keep going at it. It’s always a very difficult process. …Although the Grand Award is always so popular, I think this shows a different side of games. Unfortunately, innovativeness doesn't always link to profitability. There’s not many people who will always drink the newest version of an interesting drink. You usually go with things you’re used to. It’s always hard for this kind of innovativeness and creativity to be recognized, but if the industry loses creativity and innovation, I think the industry as a whole will slowly die. We always need new discoveries and innovations to keep the industry fresh and alive."

A second translator noted that Sakurai said he hopes players will “keep being interested in creative games even after the award is gone.”

Winners of the Game Designer Award over the last three years were Sad Owl Studios’ Viewfinder , Odd Meter’s Indika , and RPG Time: The Legend of Wright. Fans have been left saddened by this turn of events, but are hopeful that this means Sakurai will be taking time to focus on new projects — especially with all the rumors of a new Smash Bros. game that have been flying around lately.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin

Unlike the light-hearted Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles stories you may be used to, The Last Ronin takes a much, much darker turn. This graphic novel follows the story of a lone turtle looking to get revenge after the death of his brothers and master.

The graphic novel version combines the five-part miniseries of comics into one collection. The story is written by the original creators of TMNT, Kevin Eastman and Peter Laird, and is illustrated by the Escorza Brothers .

While The Last Ronin is a more recent addition to the franchise, it's actually been in the works since the early days of TMNT. The idea for a more mature turtle story was first introduced back in 1987 when the creators were just starting to get the cartoon and merchandise off the ground. The story got shelved until 2018 when the creators decided to give it the life it deserved.

Since it was first published, The Last Ronin has been widely praised. It's become so popular that there's now even a video game in the works over at PlatinumGames. If you're in the mood for a really dark (and surprisingly emotional) TMNT tale, it's definitely worth picking up this graphic novel.

If you'd prefer to enjoy the story as a more traditional book, there is a purely written adaptation available as of June 2026 . It's written by Erik Burnham and has received similarly high praise.

articles.title: Warner Bros. Reportedly Regrets Torching Zack Snyder's DC Universe and Battling With Him on Justice League
articles.summary: A Warner Bros. executive expressed regret over battling Zack Snyder on his vision for DC, according to the director.
articles.body:
A Warner Bros. executive expressed regret over battling Zack Snyder on his vision for DC, according to the director.

In a new interview with Variety , Zack Snyder spoke about the implosion of his DC universe, calling it a "low point." The director revealed that a former Warner Bros. executive told Snyder that he was "right about everything" and expressed remorse over battling him on his vision for the DC universe.

"I met with this executive at Warner Bros. who’s long gone since — I won’t say who it was — and he said to me, 'You know, Zack, I’ve got to tell you one thing: You were right about everything.' And I was like, 'That’s kind of you.' And he goes, 'We were fighting you, and in the end you were right.' [...] They did this attempt to control it — and I’m just talking about the regime that was there that’s no longer there.

"They had this massive IP that’s worth a ton, and I can understand wanting to protect it as best they could since all their jobs depended on it working, and they’d put it in the hands of a madman — or so they thought — so the part of them thinking that, and this is going to sound horrible, 'This thing that happened to Zack is a window for us to take the movie back now.'"

Warner Bros. spent years battling with Snyder on his DC universe, as the director wanted to tell darker, more grounded stories that broke the established rules of a lot of these iconic characters. Man of Steel ended with Superman snapping General Zod's neck, Batman v Superman sees Batman killing and branding people, and there were plans to turn Superman into a violent ruler of Earth in future films. Once fans started to respond negatively , WB started to push back and compromise Snyder's vision.

Snyder also noted that he's never seen the theatrical cut of Justice League, which was a Frankenstein-ed version of Snyder's original movie and another version by Joss Whedon. Whedon was brought in to lighten the film's tone, bring it under 2 hours, and also remove a variety of elements, such as the presence of Darkseid, who was seemingly being built up as DC's Thanos .

Justice League Snyder Cut: All the Known Differences From the Theatrical Version

Snyder's wife, Deborah Snyder, was a producer on his DC films and saw Whedon's cut ahead of its release. She warned him to never watch it, seemingly realizing that it would break his heart knowing it was no longer his vision. The film was critically panned, bombed at the box office, and for all intents and purposes, killed the DC universe as we knew it then. Although it would hobble along for a few more years, the synergy and cohesion that fans expected was gone, as studio heads tried to find a path forward while talent like Ben Affleck fled.

"I’ve never seen it," said Snyder. "There was a point when the movie was released that was a low point for me because the pile-on effect was so insane. Not only did I lose my daughter, but also they’ve released this version of the movie that I had nothing to do with and my name is on a movie that I didn’t make.

Snyder shot the entire film, but had to step away during post-production after his daughter committed suicide. After years of fan pressure, Snyder was able to eventually finish and release his vision of Justice Leauge, which was four hours long. While it's not for everyone, most fans agree that it is a much better movie than Whedon's cut .

DC was properly rebooted last year with James Gunn's Superman, which was followed up by 2026's Supergirl. Snyder noted he hasn't seen either, deeming his relationship to DC "too personal."

"I haven’t seen the movies," said Snyder. "It’s a little bit too personal for me. Too soon, I guess you could say. I do like James [Gunn]. And I do have an appreciation for his [vision].

Snyder has moved on from superheroes and is gearing up for a proper release of his latest passion project, The Last Photograph. IGN saw the film at TIFF and gave it a 4/10 , slamming it for a lack of substance.

"A film that points at big ideas about image-making without ever moving towards them, Zack Snyder’s passion project The Last Photograph is a languid, plodding revenge saga," reads an excerpt from the review. "Despite trying to frame beauty and brutality side by side, it’s rife with the kind of ugliness it isn’t ready to confront, rooted in dimensionless characters who are too similarly stoic to make for a meaningful or engaging journey."

articles.title: HBO Boss All But Confirms The Last of Us Show Will End With Season 3
articles.summary: The CEO of HBO says he “thinks” The Last of Us showrunner Craig Mazin has planned for the series to end on a third and final season.
articles.body:
The CEO of HBO says he “thinks” The Last of Us showrunner Craig Mazin has planned for the series to end on a third and final season.

HBO’s adaptation of Naughty Dog’s critically-acclaimed game franchise is coming to an end. At least, that’s what the Chairman and CEO of HBO and Max Content, Casey Bloys, all but admitted to Deadline during the streamer’s Emmys afterparty on Monday.

Speaking with the outlet, Bloys stated that The Last of Us Season 3 will take place in 2027, though he didn’t have a specific date to share. He also wouldn’t directly confirm whether or not it would be the show’s last season, but said he “thinks” it’s been planned as the end of the series.

“I think [showrunner] Craig [Mazin] has planned it as the final season,” he told Deadline .

The Last of Us Season 2 Episode 1: TV Show vs Game Comparison

This isn’t a huge surprise; Bloys has been indicating as much for the last year, telling Deadline in January when asked if Season 3 will be the show’s last that “it certainly seems that way, but on decisions like that, we will defer to the showrunners. So you can ask them.”

However, in May 2025, Craig Mazin was singing a decidedly different tune, saying a fourth season was necessary to wrap everything up.

“There’s no way to complete this narrative in a third season,” he told Collider at the time. "Hopefully, we’ll earn our keep enough to come back and finish it in a fourth. That’s the most likely outcome."

Season 3 of TLOU was announced before Season 2 had ever started. The show’s first season was met with critical acclaim, with IGN’s Simon Cardy scoring the show a nine out of 10 . Its second season, however, stumbled, with many viewers taking issue with Bella Ramsey’s portrayal of Ellie in the adult stage of her life. IGN scored Season 2 a seven out of 10 , with Cardy saying it was “still good, but it’s also a sequel that struggles because it’s only half of the story.”

While it’s looking more likely than ever that the show might be coming to an end next year, Naughty Dog has made it clear that it isn’t done with its flagship zombie franchise , even though it stepped back in its involvement with HBO’s screen adaptation for its third season.

"It's important for us to note that as the creator of the games, Naughty Dog is still the steward of this IP and even though this might be the end of this adaptation," Naughty Dog boss Neil Druckmann said to the Washington Post earlier this month. “We're not done with The Last of Us. There's a couple projects in the works that, when the time is right, I'm very excited to talk about."

For now, the studio is focused on its next offering, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet , which recently finished filming its performance capture in August — though its lack of an appearance at the September 2026 State of Play left some fans disappointed.

articles.title: Marvel's Wolverine Offers Up a Canonical Explanation for Why Logan's Costume Regenerates
articles.summary: Marvel's Wolverine explains why Logan's clothes can heal, just like his body.
articles.body:
Marvel's Wolverine explains why Logan's clothes can heal, just like his body.

Near the beginning of Marvel's Wolverine, Logan is gifted a proper superhero suit from Walter Langkowski. It's Wolverine's signature suit from the comics, cowl and all. Langkowski explains that his suit utilizes nano-tech, which can autorepair Logan's suit in the field. It's a clever workaround to make sure Wolverine's suit doesn't get shredded to the point of no return, leaving him to run around in the nude (though, that's not really out of character, either).

However, this isn't just any ordinary nano-tech: it's Phalanx. In Marvel lore, Phalanx are a cybernetic species that go up against the X-Men and other heroes. They use their techno-organic lifeforms to infect other species and create a hivemind. Whether this has any larger implications remains to be seen, but it's likely more of a fun way to explain things to fans using established material from the Marvel universe. In the MCU, nano-tech is extremely popular and is used prominently by Iron Man, Spider-Man, Black Panther, and the entire Avengers team in Endgame. It's nifty, though some feel like the films have begun to over-rely on it for suits.

In X-Men Origins: Wolverine, a game that Insomniac's new title takes a lot of inspiration from, Logan's wounds would also heal when out of combat. This sometimes meant that his clothes would re-generate too, but there wasn't really an in-universe reason for this, though no one seemed to care back then.

articles.summary: Joe Brammer, the CEO of Wardogs developer Bulkhead, has stated that the studio avoids hiring people that aren't willing to crunch.
articles.body:
Joe Brammer, the CEO of Wardogs developer Bulkhead, has stated that the studio avoids hiring people who aren't willing to crunch.

In an interview with The Game Business , Brammer was asked about the studio's approach to crunch. He noted that he values balance, but not in the way people may think. Instead of traditional work weeks, the team will push harder for a handful of months, but then have the opportunity to take their foot off the gas without fear of retaliation.

"For the last three months, Wardogs has been a lot more important than a lot of their family lives," said Brammer. "It has been, because that's what pays the money for them. But now Bulkhead has to acknowledge that it needs to go the other way. For example, everyone is pushing us to get console out earlier.

"We've just said, 'No, you don't understand, that's not how it's going to work. We can't push them more. We're not doing that. It's going to release in 2028 when we say it's going to release.' So, for me it's about balance and helping people and making sure they have a company where they can say, 'I'm tapping out,' and not feel like they're going to get fired for tapping out."

Brammer went on to note that it has become harder to crunch due to the team getting older and trying to start families. He stated that they initially offered 10-week paternity leave, but eventually had to ditch it because the employees' partners were struggling to handle them going back to work. Instead, Bulkhead now offers 2-weeks of paternity leave and gives half-days to employees as a way of making the transition easier for the families.

Brammer also stated that they don't hire people who actively speak out against crunch in the industry on social media, as he believes they won't be a good fit for Bulkhead.

"A lot of people who may have an issue with crunch — rightly so, I understand that issue, we always try and avoid it, but we don’t hide that this is going to happen at some point — they often don't make it in the door," he says. "We want to be known for that: this is a place you come to work hard. If you care about the work you’re making and the result of what you make here, you'll feel really valued. If you don't, you will feel slave-driven."

Brammer's belief that the team must crunch has prompted Bulkhead to create incentives for developers. The team dishes out a "meaningful amount" in bonuses and shares in the company to select employees, though not everyone is eligible.

"If we're going to be a company who says, 'we do crunch', then we have to also say, 'but you get something for it,'" he said. "We want people to know that those people who do work hard get that return, and it is life-changing."

Wardogs has already sold a whopping 2 million copies in less than a week , meaning those incentivized employees are probably (hopefully) being justly compensated. The game is sitting near the top of Steam's most played games chart and is continuing to grow as word of mouth spreads. As noted by Brammer, Wardogs is also coming to consoles in 2028, and the team is going to take its sweet time getting there.

articles.title: Every Fourth Wing Board Game Adaption You Can Buy Right Now
articles.body:
Rebecca Yarros' Empyrean series has taken the romantasy genre by storm over the past few years. With three books so far, an upcoming graphic novel, and a TV show in the works, there's never been a better time to be a fan of Fourth Wing.

And while the TV series is likely the most exciting adaptation the books will ever see, Fourth Wing has already quietly been making its way into the tabletop space over the last couple of years. There are now four Fourth Wing board games you can buy, and probably more on their way.

The rise of romantasy tabletop games is a fairly recent thing. For the Empyrean series it all began with the release of Priorities Fourth Wing Edition last year. Since then we've gotten an original strategy game and two branded Monopoly games out of the franchise. This same tabletop arc also seems to be happening for Sarah J. Maas' ACOTAR series simultaneously.

Fourth Wing: Rise of the Wingleader is the only original board game for the series so far. Created by Goliath Games, Rise of the Wingleader is a strategy board game that incorporates cards with custom artwork, dragon pieces, and a round game board. You also get a nice metal bookmark alongside the board game itself.

Priorities is a popular party game that requires players to essentially rank their "priorities" of certain topics. The Fourth Wing version of that is a re-skin of the original game and is just as straightforward. There's a huge stack of cards featuring things from the books and players pull five cards and rank them from best to worst. This is a cooperative game , so everyone in the squad is in this together.

Monopoly Deal: Fourth Wing follows the same standard rules of Monopoly Deal, but with an Emperien series glow-up. The primary goal of the game is to be the first player to successfully collect three complete property sets of different colors. Each player will also be given a Signet card that will give them a unique special ability.

Fourth Wing Monopoly functions like regular Monopoly, but with easter eggs sprinkled in from the books. Instead of the classic game pieces, there are seven different colored metal dragon pieces representing the different types of dragons in the game. This includes Violet Sorrengail's Tairn (Black) and Andarna (Golden Feathertail) as well as Xaden's Blue Daggertail Sgaeyl. The game also replaces the usual property pieces with Outposts and Strongholds which can be used to claim notable locations from the books, like the Parapet, the Gauntlet, and Aretia.

Wo Long 2: Wings of Ember, the upcoming action-soulslike sequel from Team Ninja (Nier, Ninja Gaiden), will be released on March 4, 2027 for PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S (including day one on Xbox Game Pass Ultimate), and Nintendo Switch 2. Meanwhile, a free playable alpha demo is available now on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC. The demo will only be active for a limited time, from now through September 30.

Team Ninja says that the demo includes an in-progress character creator to try out as well as online multiplayer for up to three players. "Fans can explore the open field of Changban, join forces with Liu Bei’s army in fierce battles against the pursuing forces of Cao Cao, and encounter demons inspired by legendary Chinese classics," the developer said. In addition, anyone who plays and completes the demo will unlock the Fledgling Phoenix Helmet cosmetic item for use in the full game.

The original Wo Long was released in early 2023 and our resident soulslike superfan Mitchell Saltzman thought it was great , saying, "When it comes to the clashing of melee weapons, Wo Long is among the best in the genre, full stop." We also had it at #6 in our list of top-10 soulslikes published later in 2023.

Wo Long 2 was announced at this year's Xbox Showcase.

articles.title: Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter Captures Everything That Made the Original so Endearing While Giving It an Impressive Makeover
articles.summary: An impressive remake which captures everything that made the original so endearing.
articles.body:
One of the biggest hurdles of the Trails series was how to introduce its world to new players when almost every game is interconnected through multiple follow-up entries. After all, the original The Legend of Heroes: Trails in the Sky subseries was only on PC and older handhelds like the PSP. Fortunately, developer Falcom remedied that with the excellent Trails in the Sky 1st Chapter remake last year – finally, an approachable way to start where the trail began with a slick 3D makeover and updated gameplay. Swiftly following up with a remake of Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter, this RPG retains all of the best qualities of the original version, such as its story, side quests, and characters, while simultaneously giving it that visual and gameplay overhaul to fit modern standards.

Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter picks up right where its predecessor ends with our bubbly and confident heroine, Estelle Bright. Now that her adoptive brother and best friend Joshua Bright suddenly recalled his true origins and has disappeared, Estelle is dead set on finding him and bringing him home. It also digs deeper and fleshes out the cultish revelations that were unearthed towards the end of 1st Chapter. As a result, it gives 2nd Chapter heavier stakes from onset, but also with the emotionally resonant edge that keeps you invested.

The characters are equally zany too, and they’re brimming with personality. Estelle’s, ahem, bright , demeanor contrasts nicely with Joshua’s now brooding mood. The two theater nerds in Olivier and the villainous Blueblanc face off in a duel of overindulgent poetry to see who can out-cringe each other. It’s all entertaining to watch and the experience is bolstered thanks to the addition of full voice acting (whereas the original Trails in the Sky games only had voice acting for the combat). In these Sky remakes, the script and story are brought to life even more so with those original voice actors of Estelle and Joshua reprising their roles. It feels like a full-circle moment, especially for fans who’ve stuck with Trails since the beginning.

2nd Chapter is virtually a faithful 1:1 recreation of the original in terms of story structure and side quests, so you’ll be running around Liberl Kingdom going through the same cities and locations as you did in 1st Chapter. While that might seem like a rehash, the order in which you visit them in this sequel is rearranged. Along with a completely different slate of side quests to tackle from the previous adventure, it makes this journey feel much less like a retread and more like revisiting an old home.

There aren’t any multiple divergent storylines that cross together with later entries like Trails Beyond the Horizon and Trails Into Reverie , which also came with a roguelite dungeon where all the characters could interact outside of the story. It works in 2nd Chapter’s favor as it isn’t unnecessarily bogged down with extra story content simply for the sake of having something new. It’s a streamlined adventure that’s easy to follow without superfluous bloat that some later Trails entries would suffer from.

That being said, the pacing in the last chapter before heading into the finale is a bit stunted since you're required to backtrack through previous locations one final time due to story reasons. The issue is that almost all of your fast travel points that you unlocked before disappear, and you’ll have to activate them again, which makes this particular bump in the road a slog.

Leaning into a stylized anime-inspired art direction with these remakes brings bolder colors and a new vision for familiar worlds, however. The transition between combat phases are smoother, and the use of more camera angles and sharp cuts give attacks and crafts more cinematic flair. You can see close ups of every character’s fierce facial expressions as they shout out and execute their attacks in ways that you never could with the top-down sprites of the original. The new character models and animations give the story some extra life, whether it’s the party enjoying themselves while exploring the world or fighting for their lives against an all-powerful foe.

The character animations look a lot less awkward in both gameplay and cutscenes, and in critical junctures, they do a lot to add weight for its more serious, pivotal moments. Along with that, the political machinations and turmoil that dictate its world, and the origins of what you see further in the series, feel more fully realized. And the story here in Sky 2nd Chapter strikes a wonderful momentum for concluding Estelle's and Joshua’s character arcs cleanly and concisely without prolonging them – it’s something that other protagonists suffered a bit from in later Trails sagas.

This remake benefits from 13 games and over 20 years of iterations, taking the framework of existing gameplay systems from Trails games that came before. While the original version was purely turn-based, 2nd Chapter quite heavily borrows the real-time and turn-based hybrid system that the Trails into Daybreak entries started. You can attack enemies in-real time in the field (Quick Battles) to whittle them down and stun them to gain an advantage, then immediately transition to the main turn-based combat (Command Battles). Some Trails purists may not like the change to hybrid combat, but it’s the biggest change that makes it stand out from the original.

A significant difference in the Sky remakes is the addition of Brave Points (BP), which were introduced in the Cold Steel saga – you accumulate them by landing critical hits, stunning enemies, or hitting stunned enemies. Depending on how many BP you spend, you can initiate Brave Attacks which include follow-up hits from an ally, coordinated chain strikes, or an all-out group burst like that in Persona for additional damage. It makes 2nd Chapter’s combat much more engaging and explosive than the original’s.

2nd Chapter also cleverly merges and evolves the hybrid and BP mechanics together. In the Daybreak games, Van and his crew would just throw shards to deal extra damage if a Command battle started with an advantage. However, when you enter them with an advantage in Sky 2nd Chapter, you can launch a preemptive Brave Attack, letting you start off the fight with a powerful Brave Chain or Burst move. It’s impressive that 2nd Chapter doesn’t merely just copy and paste combat mechanics from previous Trails entries, but further refines them into something more satisfying.

BP can also be consumed during Quick battles in the form of a Brave Rush, which are powerful hits that deal exceedingly more stun damage, allowing you to enter into an advantage state faster. It’s helpful on larger enemies who are more resilient to stun, but there’s a strategic trade off. Since Brave Rush uses BP, you’ll enter the Command phase with fewer BP, meaning you might not have enough to initiate a preemptive Brave Attack. Give-and-take compromises like these ensure that the battle system remains relatively balanced and challenging.

Brave Rushes weren’t in Daybreak’s hybrid battles, and so the Sky remakes have a dedicated button for it. While it’s a welcome addition to the combat, it’s actually also the tipping point that makes the control scheme for Quick battles a bit unwieldy. In particular, all modern Trails games have a high-speed mode, which as its name suggests, accelerates overall game speed at any time. In previous games, this was a simple one-button toggle on the controller, but in these remakes, you have to press the left and right bumpers at the same time to toggle it. As a longtime Trails player, I’ve been conditioned to the one-button toggle for high-speed mode so it's a bit of an annoying change, but it’s a very miniscule problem in the grand scheme of things.

As with all other Trails games, the timeline mechanic makes its welcome return once again, clearly showing the turn order of allies and enemies. Randomized turn bonuses continue to add variability, augmenting the abilities of whomever’s turn icon is lined up with it, whether friend or foe. These can range from automatic HP recovery, guaranteed critical hits, to eliminating both casting time and cost (called Zero Arts). Sure, beating enemies is gratifying, but much of that feeling comes from manipulating the timeline order through different spells and special attacks (called Crafts) while making the most of their innate effects.

Is there a critical hit icon next to a monster casting a spell? Agate’s Draguna Blast can inflict Impede to interrupt spellcasting. The enemy will still be able to land a critical hit with whatever their next non-casting attack will be, but at least they won’t be able to fire off that devastating spell. You’ve postponed the inevitable, giving you a moment of reprieve in this volatile yet orderly battle system. But what if you don’t want to leave it to chance, you can use Zin’s True Heralding Fist to inflict Delay, which pushes down bonuses farther down the timeline so that it’ll land on someone else, preferably one of your allies. It’s instances like these where you have to balance dishing out as much damage as possible with managing the combat timeline for bonuses that could change the tide of battle.

Despite Daybreak 2 making it easier to steal bonuses compared to its predecessor, the Sky remakes simplify it further. For example, certain offensive Crafts like Estelle’s Comet have a “Steal Bonus” effect, which lets her do just that. While not every character has a regular Craft with that effect, all offensive S-Crafts (ultimate attacks) do, giving every character the ability to steal bonuses in some capacity. It’s a really useful change because it synergizes well with the fact that you can now stack multiple bonuses onto one character. You can have HP recovery, critical hit, and Zero Arts icons activate all in one turn if you play your cards right. Playing around with delay and stealing effects adds a fun twist, with trade-off being your house of cards potentially collapsing because enemies can also steal bonuses and undo all your hard work. Don’t get too greedy!

2nd Chapter uses Daybreak’s free roam during Command battles, so your team is able to move as much as they want around the battlefield without using up a turn. It’s crucial to position your characters properly because now everyone’s Crafts have been updated with new effects, including the aforementioned Steal Bonus effect. For example, Kloe’s Kämpfer in the original game only lowered enemies’ strength and defense stats, but in this remake, it now also does extra damage when striking an enemy from the side as opposed to the front or back. It’s small changes like these that help 2nd Chapter feel modern and up to date with recent Trails entries.

The Orbment system continues to be a great way to customize magic spells and perks for each character. These remakes surprisingly mirror the original’s system as it doesn’t have Cold Steel's broken buildcrafting or Daybreak’s multitude of passive Shard abilities. Here, where you place your elemental gems (called Quartz) determines which spells a certain character can use. Whereas in Daybreak everyone had the same four different lines in their Orbments to slot Quartz in, 2nd Chapter’s set up is more rigid

Magically-oriented characters can have their Quartz setup to unlock higher tier spells, as opposed to those who are physical-focused. This stricter system reflects a much more old-school RPG approach as if to have specialized character classes. It’s more straightforward to understand, and initially feels a little underdeveloped coming from the openness and flexibility of Orbment systems in other Trails entries. But in a field of revisions, it’s admirable to at least see one aspect of gameplay in these Sky remakes that staunchly sticks to its roots.
